utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I would like to verify first whether the videolink is functioning well. Can you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, good morning, Your Honours. We can see and hear you clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see and hear you clearly as well. Therefore, after I have reminded Mr. Kelecevic that, and please listen well, Mr. Kelecevic, you're still bound by the solemn declaration; that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. You're still bound by that solemn declaration. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to Kotor Varos. The 5th Corps Brigade responsible for Kotor Varos was the 122nd Brigade under Colonel Bosko Peulic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02660.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the minutes of the 13th Session of the National Defence Council of Kotor Varos municipality, held on the 7th of April. Looking under item 1, we see that one of the recorded speakers is Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic, described as "the commander of the JNA unit based in our municipality." Now this is a reflection that by early April 1992 the 122nd Brigade had been deployed back to Bosnia from Croatia and was responsible for, among other places, the area of Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7479. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When the VRS came into being, the VRS unit responsible for Kotor Varos, this brigade, became the 22nd Brigade and Colonel Peulic remained the commander; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02596.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, Peulic's unit participated in moving non-Serbs out of the Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I mean, what it is that you mean. Moving Serbs where?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Moving non-Serbs from Kotor Varos out of the Republika Srpska; right? Colonel Peulic's unit participated in that.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was his area of responsibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is an extract from the minutes of the 100th Session of the War Presidency in Kotor Varos held on the 16th of October, 1992. You don't claim that you were still in an information vacuum in Doboj at that point, do you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was precisely the month of October when I was busy concerning Brod; that is to say, facing the Sava. It was only on the 7th of October that Brod was liberated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, one of your previous questions was the participation of Peulic's unit in moving non-Serbs out. You then asked the witness to confirm that. He said: "Yes. That was his area of responsibility ..." But it was not very clear whether he also confirmed your proposition that Peulic's unit was involved in the moving out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I recognise that, Mr. President. In the interest of the efficiency because it's addressed in the documents that I'm using, I'd moved on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I understand why you did not insist on an answer at that point in time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this is the 16th of October after the 7th when Brod fell, and at the bottom of this page, in both languages, we see president Nedjelko Dj pointed out that: An International Red Cross team had been in the area again yesterday, that the negotiators had gone to Vecici too, that the initial results from Vecici were not favourable, that they'd had met the other side's representatives, (Bastina), that a list containing the names of 12- to 1500 people had been compiled, that this will require about 30 buses, and intensified activity relating to move out should be expected. I'm going to turn now to P3715, an excerpt of another meeting of the Kotor Varos War Presidency held two days later on the 18th of October. Now, in the middle of the middle of the first paragraph we read that: The same president of the War Presidency mentions that as for the action of surrendering weapons and the moving from the territory of Kotor Varos, the drive and all activities had been conducted on the orders of the government and the Presidency of Republika Srpska. And in the second paragraph, that: Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic stressed that he had participated from the very beginning (11 June) in preparing all the activities, that there was no straying from the general policy and goals, stop the fratricidal war in these parts, prevent the entry of armed unit, disband all paramilitary units, allowing only the VRS to exist and operate. Now, when he says he participated in preparing all the activities in the context of their discussion of moving people out, what he is saying is, as I put to you a moment ago, his unit participated in moving people out, moving non-Serbs out, of Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he said that he participated but not on his own. The MUP forces took part to a considerable degree, and they were legal in the area of responsibility of Bosko Peulic and along that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the second page in both languages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us where you read this in the document? Perhaps we go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't read it in the document at all. I know what the position of the corps command was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, were you present during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not present. I was busy. I'm telling you, I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you've answered that question. So therefore, if you say I think that he said, you have neither a basis for that in the document nor any personal observation, not being present. Is that correctly understood? Please proceed. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like the document to be read, not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the part was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because whenever it's interpreted, it's not correct and it's confusing the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take exception to Mr. Lukic's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a sweeping statement, that whenever it's interpreted that it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, not again --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do not interrupt me again, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the relevant part was read literally. If you think it was not, please tell us where Mr. Traldi misread --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that the witness's headphones be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. He heard -- Mr. Traldi -- needs to hear the rest because otherwise he would be confused.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but [Overlapping speakers] here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am at a point to consider with my colleagues to take measures if --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Against the Prosecution who is not reading the document but interpreting it wrongly. You should take the action against him, not against me. I'm trying to correct these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stop immediately. Sit down, Mr. Lukic. Sit down, please. When Mr. Traldi addresses me in order to ask the Court that the witness takes off his earphones, he's perfectly entitled to do so. That's where you intervened. The problem is since there are overlapping speakers that perhaps not always the transcript says anything. Could the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again please. If the witness takes off his earphones, that is exclusively for the purpose of the witness not following our discussions. If something wrongly was read to the witness, after we've discussed it, when the witness puts on his earphones again, he'll be informed about any mistake and it will be corrected. And I think you should be confident that that's the procedurally proper way to proceed. And that's what I'm going to do now. Could the witness take off his earphones. Mr. Lukic, where do you think that what Mr. Traldi read is an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Last paragraph on the first page in B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. Let's have a look. And where do we find it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was implied that something illegal was done. First sentence says, I'll read in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go to the relevant page. It is which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's probably the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the page in the transcript, Mr. Lukic. Because that's where we find what Mr. Traldi read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The question was really long. And it encompasses two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Where did he misstate the evidence in the transcript? I give you time to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 4, line 5. And next document continues from the line 13 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's start with you say page 4, line 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. What's wrongly quoted there?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nothing is quoted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. What is misrepresented there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That -- I'll read in B/C/S. [Interpretation] "Colonel Peulic, taking the floor again, pointed out that one should not give up on the position and agreements reached concerning the surrender of weapons" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Lukic. First of all, if you read something which you say Mr. Traldi misrepresented, I'd like first to know exactly what part of the transcript we should look at in order to find out whether your are right or not. What in the transcript was said, which you then later will tell us why it is inconsistent with the text of the document before us. What did he say that is wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was implied. Nothing was quoted. I cannot find you what is quoted wrongly. Nothing was quoted. I'm trying to quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where does it misrepresent?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 4, line 5 until line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I read there: "So this is the 16th of October after the 7th when Brod fell." Now, that is not in the document. I think that's an introduction by Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not wrong. And at the bottom of this page in both languages, we see President Nedjelko, let me see, pointed out that an International Red Cross team had been in the area yesterday. Is that right or is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I was trying to find it in the document that's on our screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I saw it once, but Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Previous document that we have on our screens, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The previous document, okay. That's agreed. Please do not overlap. So it's agreed that that was in the previous document. But there's no dispute about it. That the negotiators had gone to Vecici too. I think that was also read from that document. That the initial results from Vecici were not favourable. Perhaps we move to the previous document so as to be able to verify every single.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have back 65 ter 02596.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. There we have it at the bottom, Mr. Lukic. "President Nedjelko D pointed out that..." Okay. We'll now continue because what we've read until now I think is almost literally if not literally at all what is presented in this document. "... that the initial results from Vecici were not favourable..." Is that what the document says? "... that they had the other side's representative (Bastina)," which is literally in the document. "That a list containing the names of 12 to 1500 people had been compiled, that this will require about 30," and then it says "expected," but it's about buses apparently. Now you said there was a misquote from lines 5 to 12. Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was suggested? Look at the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That there was something illegal. It's enough to omit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's misleading if you omit the crucial part: That there is agreement - there is agreement - and he wants to respect the agreement. That's the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the proper way of dealing with this is that you invite Mr. Traldi under those circumstance or you address us to invite Mr. Traldi to include the next paragraph as well. If Mr. Traldi does so, the problem is resolved. If Mr. Traldi does not, then you have a possibility in re-examination to present the proper context --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's next first sentence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's nothing -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything is in this next sentence, Your Honour. Everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's your position, and you may present your position in re-examination. Mr. Lukic, you presented a statement of the witness in which, without any source, without any further explanation, he says something about Kotor Varos. Mr. Traldi may explore that. If you think he is doing that out of context, you have an opportunity to correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But then I will really need a lot of time to correct everything that was misrepresented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what you should have done, Mr. Lukic, you should have presented a statement of the witness which gives proper sources and which is not just sweeping statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that for the time being. I have two further observations to be made. First, if you stand, Mr. Lukic, you wait for being given an opportunity to address us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should not object to questions made by the Bench unless there is an obvious error made by the Bench and if you want to gently point at that possibility, you have an opportunity to do so. But apart from that, no objections against questions by the Bench. And again, whatever happens, re-examination is the proper time to deal with the matter. If that's clear, then we'll continue after we have invited the witness to put on his earphones again. And perhaps he can see me. Mr. Traldi, I leave it in your hands. You know what Mr. Lukic invited you to do. I leave it to you whether you want to follow that invitation, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have P3715 back, just to complete my questions about that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, I want to return to the last thing you said. Now, you said based on your knowledge in the corps command the MUP had also participated in this moving people out of Kotor Varos. Do I correctly understand your evidence that both the MUP and Colonel Peulic's unit participated in this moving out of a large number of people from Kotor Varos after the visit by the Red Cross team to these Muslim and Croat villages and an agreement on moving those people out was reached. That's what you know; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I know that, for the most part, the MUP forces or, rather, the civilian authorities were the mainstays of these activities; the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency of the municipality of Kotor Varos, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we can have page 2 of this document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see it's Slobodan Z speaking, and just so you know it's the Prosecution's position that's Slobodan Zupljanin, battalion commander in Peulic's brigade, and he says that, among other things: "... thus far everybody had taken part in activities, including Momcilo Komljenovic, and Savo Tepic, who is also absent. All activities were agreed bearing in mind --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Traldi please give us a reference in B/C/S as to where he is reading from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's the top of the page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you skipped half a line, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right. It starts in the middle of the second sentence at the words "thus far." And I'll start reading again: "... thus far, everybody had taken part in activities, including Momcilo Komljenovic, and Savo Tepic, who is also absent. All activities were agreed bearing in mind directives from higher organs: The Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and the Presidency of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the directives from the Main Staff, those were relayed to Peulic' unit through the 1st Krajina Corps command, right? They would issue a directive to you, you would pass down an order to Colonel Peulic's unit.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31380.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this an issue of Novi Vjesnik, dated two days later, 20 October, 1992. We read and it's the middle of the page on the left in B/C/S: "A vehicle of the International Red Cross is escorting 350 Croatian and Muslim soldiers and thousands of civilians liberated by exchange - along a winding road through Central Bosnia - from Kotor Varos to the free territory in Travnik." And this is an example of what we discussed yesterday, exchanges resulting in people being moved out of the RS, non-Serbs being moved out of RS and into Muslim and Croat territory; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me whether this is correct? This kind of moving out?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I asked you a very specific question. This is an example of what we discussed yesterday, exchanges resulting in the moving out of non-Serbs from the RS into Muslim and Croat territory; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 02596 and 31380 as public exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They shall be assigned Exhibit P7480 and P7481, respectively. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31913.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is an article titled: "From the War Log," in a publication known as Vlasicki Vidici from the 19th of November, 1993. If we turn to page 2 in the English and the top of the far right column on page 1 in the B/C/S, we see the words: "Blockades of Kotor Varos, SDS takes over power." When Colonel Peulic said his unit had participated in all the activities from the 11th of June, from the beginning, this is the beginning he is talking about, the blockade and take-over of Kotor Varos on the 11th of June; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what he had in mind. As a soldier, though, I do know that he participated within his area of responsibility in the implementation of the tasks involved. This was also definitely a part of that and it was done together with the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7482. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7482 is admit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We saw Vecici mentioned in one of the documents we looked at earlier. At the end of October and early November 1992, the 1st Krajina Corps was regularly reporting to the Main Staff about negotiations with the residents of Vecici; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mladic was in the 1st Krajina Corps's area of responsibility at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say whether he was there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution have P2884.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an excerpt of the minutes from the meeting of the Kotor Varos War Presidency on the 2nd of November, 1992. We see under point II, President Djekanovic said that Colonel Bogojevic would come during the day and that Mladic had ordered that any agreement with him regarding, what we see in the English, Vucic should be implemented. So Colonel Bogojevic, that's the corps's assistant commander for security; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now if we turn to page 3 in the English and 2 in the B/C/S, we see a continuation of that session. We see Colonel Bogojevic, Major Trivic, Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic, Captain Zupljanin and Captain Balaban are all present. Captain Balaban was also an officer in the corps's security organ; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a reserve of officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see that Colonel Bogojevic informed all present that he had received explicit orders from General Mladic that no one was to be allowed to leave Vecici until the unconditional surrender of weapons was completed. This reflects Mladic's taking personal involvement, personal control of what was to be done regarding the negotiations with the Vecici residents; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that Mr. Mladic took part personally. I simply don't know. I can't confirm whether he was there at the time. If it was in November, I was still at the command post in Doboj, or, rather, at Trebava.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I hadn't suggested that he took part in the negotiations personally. What I'm putting to you is what we see here is he is clearly giving personal direction, taking personal control of what the negotiation position is going to be; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could agree, but I cannot assert that it was the case. I simply don't remember and don't know. I don't remember any such words being uttered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You are aware, though, that in the 48 hours after this session, approximately 150 Muslim men from Vecici were taken prisoner by the VRS and murdered in and around the Grabovica school in Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about it from reports. But as far as I know, again, it had to do with the civilian authorities and their treatment of those people in the school at Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Prisoners surrender to the VRS, they're held by the VRS in a school, they're murdered. It's the VRS's responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assert that. I don't know if the school was secured by the army or civilian authorities, i.e., the police or the MUP. I can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, first you said as far as you know it had to do with the civilian authorities. Now you say you don't know who secured the school. You immediately tried to ascribe responsibility to the civilian authorities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please do not interrupt Mr. Traldi when he puts a question. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You tried to ascribe responsibility to the civilian authorities even though you do not know, as you confirmed, who secured them because you know this was a terrible, terrible crime; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime did take place. I don't know who was securing the school at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it's not an answer to the question. But, Mr. Traldi, apparently the witness has seen some reports and that's all apparently what he knows. I think we've seen some of those reports as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, it's for the Chamber further to interpret the evidentiary material. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to Sanski Most, about which I will be very brief. The primary brigade in Sanski Most was the 6th Brigade under both the JNA and the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The commander was Branko Basara, both before and after the transformation; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was removed after a while and replaced by Colonel Nikola Kajtez. I don't recall the date, but I do know that the corps command ordered the change in the command of the 6th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32460.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a report dated the 6th of March, 1993, from operational group 2 command, and we see it comes from the commander, Branko Basara. So you said he was removed. In fact, he was put in command of an operational group. And as with Colonel Arsic's transfer to head OG Doboj, this was promotion; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not hand over his duties at this time. I can't really say when. I said that there was a change in the brigade command. A brigade commander, in addition to his duties, also had the duties of commander of the Tactical Group 3. I don't know. I can't remember now when Basara was removed from the position of brigade commander, the 6th Brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you very simply is as after the destruction of Muslim villages that we discussed briefly yesterday in Sanski Most by the 6th Brigade, Colonel Basara was given command of an operational group which comprised several brigades. That's the truth, right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by what I said. He was the brigades commander, and at the same time he was the commander of Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7483. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Witness, you earlier said that a brigade commander in addition to his duties also had the duties of commander of Tactical Group 3, whereas in your most recent answer you referred to Tactical Group 2. At least that's how it was translated to us, interpreted to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Tactical Group 3. There were several.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32174.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, you know that after those destructions of Muslim villages by the 6th Brigade, large numbers of Muslims and Croats moved out of Sanski Most; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that they moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now these are the conclusions of the Sanski Most Municipal Assembly in 1993, adopting the municipal census. Turning to page 6 in the English, 7 in the B/C/S, we see the figures for various years. Under Orthodox in 1991, we see just over 25.000; 1993, almost 28.000; we see Muslims have gone from over 28.000 to just over 4.000; Catholics, over 4.000 to just over 1.000. So over 25.000 non-Serbs had fled Sanski Most after the destruction of their villages; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say how many. As the Chief of Staff, I wasn't involved in this. I was engaged on combat operations. This was the domain of the assistant commander for civilian protection. If this was the case, then I'll take it at face value.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7484. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you know that in Prijedor and Kljuc as well, the municipalities we discussed yesterday, large numbers of Muslims and Croats left those municipalities, fled those municipalities after the operations and the crimes we discussed; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, finally, sir, you say in your statement that prisoners from the Prijedor camps were transferred to Manjaca. You don't mention this in your statement, but several prisoners were killed in that transport by members of the Prijedor police; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. I can only confirm that when they arrived at the gate of Manjaca camp, there were several people dead on the trucks. I know about that. The camp warden refused to take them over. He said that they should be returned, that he would only take over living and healthy people. Thus, the bodies were returned, but I don't know where. Therefore, my answer is the army did not secure the transport of prisoners to Manjaca. Again, it was done by the civilian authorities, i.e., members of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I invite you to carefully listen to the question because there was no suggestion in the question that they were killed by the army. Mr. Traldi, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, sir, I take it we agree that they were killed by the Prijedor police; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now my second observation, Mr. Traldi, would be the following: That your question was not unambiguous. Exactly by the Prijedor police, whether that refers to the transport or to the killing is not entirely clear, I think, in the language you used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I take it we agree that they were killed by members of the Prijedor police; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my presumption as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And none of the camp guards from the military police battalion attached to the corps command were disciplined for just allowing this to happen, were they?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that anything of the sort happened. He simply did not allow them to enter the facility at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the corps command had lists of the people who were detained at Manjaca; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command had very orderly lists with the particulars of the people held at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the transfer from Prijedor camps to Manjaca, that occurred after the first visit by international journalists to the Prijedor camps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I didn't have time to read the newspapers at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A Defence witness named Milovan Milutinovic said that you and General Talic ordered him to accompany the journalists. Was he lying?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If General Talic told him to do that, it wasn't my custom to say anything following him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But if he mentioned your name. Your evidence is that's not true; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not saying it isn't true. What I don't know is whether Milutinovic received any such order, if I may so, from me or, rather, instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Witness, if you say you don't know whether you gave such an order, a minute ago you said you wouldn't know whether something happened after a visit of the journalists because you didn't read the newspapers. But, of course, there is some friction between giving an order to do something and telling us that you didn't know because you had not read the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said that bearing in mind what happened in front of the gate concerning the reception of those prisoners and their entry to Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that is what you intended to say, then it was not an answer to the question because the question was whether those prisoners were transferred to Manjaca after the Prijedor camps had been visited by journalists. That was the issue. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you know, in fact, that that was the context. You know it was right after the Prijedor camps had been visited by journalists because you issued orders about that visit; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the corps command, i.e., the organs of the corps command who were tasked with dealing with Manjaca, issued instructions and regulations about the treatment of POWs and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- internal rules of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, stop. That's evidence you've provided already. It is not in any way a response to my question. You issued orders regarding the journalists' visits to the Prijedor camps in August 1992 that a moment ago you said you didn't know anything about because you didn't read the papers; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never issued orders. If something had been ordered previously by the commander, and I see that Mr. Milutinovic mentions having received an order from General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you are not exactly copying what Mr. Traldi told you. Mr. Traldi told you that Mr. Milutinovic had told this Court that such orders were given by General Talic and you. Are you saying that that's not what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I say that I don't remember communicating with Milutinovic whatsoever. In any case, whenever the commander issued an order, I did not issue a different one. I simply implemented his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which could mean that you pass on the order to your subordinates. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember whether I passed it on. It was the duty of other organs, those in charge of morale and security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, you knew about this context, everybody knew about this context because the Main Staff had issued orders to get those camps ready for the visit that were passed down to the 43rd Brigade through the corps command; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those ICRC visits and the visits of other international organisations were at times announced and at others time unannounced. I can't say now which one was or was not announced. It was up to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Two weeks after this visit, ICRC access was cut off for a period of about a week while the Manjaca prisoners were processed; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that the date is correct. But if there was any processing done at the time, I suppose any visits were disallowed. I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- You earlier were asked about -- to prepare the camps for visits of journalists and you were asked about that. And then you answered about visited by the ICRC and other international organisations. Could you also answer the question in respect of the visit of journalists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't. I don't know the period. I wasn't familiar at all with the visit of journalists to Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't discuss that directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the Chamber has received quite some substantial and detailed evidence about these matters, and this witness apparently was either not involved or has no recollection of being involved or what his involvement was. Therefore, I suggest that you consider to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. And I see we're at the time for the break. I think I'm very near the end and can be most efficient if I have a few minutes to reorganise, but I wouldn't expect to be more than a few minutes in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break now. We resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness takes off his earphones for a second. Thank you. Mr. Lukic, the Chamber unanimously finds that we need to react to your behaviour yesterday and today. And as a matter of fact, the Court would have expected apologies which were not expressed. Sufficient guidance has been given to you by now how you should deal with the matters you wanted to raise, though in an inappropriate way. If it happens again, I'll have to use my priority button and will switch off your microphone if it happens again. I leave it to that for the time being, and I'm confident that it will not happen again. We'll proceed. Could the witness put his earphones on again. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just a few more questions, General. First, the activities we've looked at of the 1st Krajina Corps and other Bosnian Serb forces in the Bosnian Krajina, the detention of Muslim and Croat civilians, their removal through exchange, destruction of villages and moving out of the residents, killing of the residents, the corridor operation as well, those were part of how those forces implemented the goals articulated in the first and second strategic objectives as well as in General Gvero's proclamation about the war that we saw on Monday; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally, sir, I want to step back in time. When did you first meet General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladic is a classmate of mine. We've known each other from school. We attended the academy together from 1961 to 1965, graduated together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Mr. Van hooydonk to play an audio-clip, 65 ter 32715A, from your interview. CLSS has confirmed, so we'll only need to play it once. Just for Your Honour's reference, the clip includes consecutive interpretation done at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 32715A. In CLSS's review, they've made a couple of small edits which do not change, I'd submit, the portions I intend to rely on. Those edits reflect that the transcript we've -- due to those edits the transcript we've uploaded reflects CLSS's view of the most precise translation of the witness's words rather than just the consecutive interpretation that's on the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you'll rely on that version in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Reporter: Thank you, General. What kind of commander was General Mladic? "[Interpretation] [Voice-over] As I said, we were in school together, at the academy together. We were in class together from 1961 until 1965. I didn't know him well then because he came from a vocational school to the academy, and I, I came from a military, secondary military school, but we did know each other. They knew me better than I knew them because I played football and things like that. "They knew me better than I knew them. We really didn't stay in touch later on. Milovanovic knows him very well. They served together in Macedonia. That is, the 3rd Military District. I only met him once he arrived in Knin. First he came as operations officer, then he was Chief of Staff, and then the corps commander, and while -- while I was in Sarajevo in the 2nd Military District for those two months, he was the commander of the Knin Corps which was part of the 2nd Military District. If you ask me on a personal level, I think he was very decisive, very energetic. I think he went through all the phases of the ranks, the command duties, and operational staff duties. I think he's -- he's difficult to work with. That's what I mean. "Reporter: Why was he acquainted --"

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir I, just have one question: Do you stand by the portion of your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor that we just heard? And, sorry, we've lost a question in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I respond now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I take it that you expect the witness to respond your question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything I said then, I stand by that. I didn't quite understand the translation of the last sentence or the last sentence or two? I don't know if it changes the substance, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to re-ask you that last question just for the clarity of our record. After you'd explained that he was difficult to work with, you were asked: "Is he a brutal man?" and you responded: "That's what I mean." Do you stand by that portion of your interview as well?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the word "okrutan," "cruel" is not right. He is energetic. I said that at the very beginning, that he is energetic, and he perseveres in his orders. "Okrutan," "cruel," that would not be the adequate word. I would withdraw that from that text.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32715A. It's just the page on the screen, and that completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7485. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7485 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to put on the record that we stopped the audio at 11 minutes, 30.4 seconds, and the last question was not heard when we listened to the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least not in the interpretation. Because I do remember that just before we stopped, we heard "why" which seems to be the question following the question about the personality of Mr. Mladic, and I also wondered -- I don't think we listened for 11 minutes to the -- to the audio. Therefore, Mr. Traldi, at what point in time did we start? I missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 8.41, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 8.41 up to 11 minutes, 30.4 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And 8.41 refers to this particular tape from the several tapes that were made of that audio-recorded interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And together with the audio we receive the transcription and also the corrected transcription, if I may say so. Mr. Lukic, you announced already that you would have questions in re-examination. Therefore, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I do have questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day once again, Mr. Kelecevic. Maybe there was an overlap. Good day once again, Mr. Kelecevic.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something now so that we do it in the right order. Your role in 1991 related to the corridor and what effect that had on your knowledge about other things that were happening at that time in Bosnia-Herzegovina. First, I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that you meant 1992. Not 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I meant 1992. I do apologise. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to pause a bit between questions and answers so that the interpreters could interpret everything we're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My microphone was on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that at the far end of the videolink, at least on our screen, it's indicated that the microphone is off. Mr. Registrar, could you please verify. Could the representative of the Registry at the far end confirm that the microphone is on or is it off? I get no response to that at this moment, whereas I now see that the witness apparently is --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I'm afraid we've lost the audio on the English channel. We're trying to reactivate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I again seek the assistance of the witness again to say that we'll wait until it has been restored.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since communication with the far end is not only difficult through the microphone system but also by telephone, we'll take a short break. Everyone is requested to remain standby. We hope to resume within a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 11.09 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's start with testing the videolink. Mr. Registrar at the far end of the videolink, could you confirm that you can see us and that you can hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour, we can see and hear you now clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see and hear you as well. Therefore, Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kelecevic, you mentioned that on Mondays you attended meetings of the staff or rather the command of the 1st Corps. Was it every Monday that you attended these meetings?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From April until December 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Attending these collegium meetings, that was on Mondays. But it depended on my commitments at the command post where I was from the 28th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did Operation Corridor end?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operation Corridor, it can be said that it ended when the 1st Corps linked up with the eastern Bosnian forces, and that is the liberation of Bosanski Brod on the 7th of October, 1992. However, quite a bit remained unclear there. There were still tasks to be carried out, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the combat end in relation to the corridor in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat never ended. How do I put this? It's not that there were organised attacks all the time, but as we soldiers would say, there were always provocations in all sectors, north and south.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Corps, did it suffer any losses?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Corps responded to that fire, enemy fire, against the Serb forces in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Corps, the 1st Krajina Corps, did it sustain any losses at the corridor?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Losses in those moments, if you're referring to the end of October, that is, there were losses that were lesser but they were still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us now where your command posts were, where you were from the 28th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks on our screen as if the microphone at the far end of the videolink has been switched off, and I further put on the record that the video is sometimes interrupted, if only for split seconds. Witness, could you indicate, give me a signal whether you still hear me through the B/C/S channel? I saw that you said something. If you hear me, could you just raise your hand for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apparently the witness hears us. Apparently the registrar at the far end of the videolink does not hear us, and apparently the microphone is either switched off or is not functioning, and the video is of bad quality. We take another break to see whether it can be restored. Everyone is expected to remain standby. --- Break taken at 11.24 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While everyone is still working on the quality of the videolink connection, until that has been -- until any improvement has been achieved, the Chamber would use the time dealing with procedural matters which are already, for quite some time, outstanding.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, if I may interrupt, we have established connection by an alternative route. So I think we can proceed for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll skip my plans. Let's use the videolink as long as it is good. Mr. Lukic, it's not easy for you, but give it another try.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, let's give it one more try. Please tell us where your command posts were between the 28th of April and December 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first command post, which was improved, or makeshift, so to speak, was some 15 kilometres away from Prnjavor, between Prnjavor town and Derventa. The place is called Vrelo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please stop. Please tell us what kind of communications you had at Vrelo? What kind of communications means.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean communication with the corps command?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio communication and a telephone line with the command post in Stara Gradiska in Slavonia. That was because my commander was still there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was it that did you not have that a command post should?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that command post, I did not have the possibility to receive dispatches, at least not all of them, and there were no radio relay communications that were necessary at the time. We only had them later, in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you move from that command post; and, if so, where to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The sound is too poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please stop. We are losing you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I take it that you also cannot hear the witness in his own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's very hard, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there's not a reliable --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Interruptions, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Witness, we'll deal with other matters while everyone is working hard to restore the quality of the audio and video connection. Please take off your earphones for a moment. We'll continue with other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the skipped plans are activated again. I'll start with some remaining issues from the testimony of Dragisa Masal. I start with P7227. On the 18th of March of this year, P7227 was marked for identification pending a revised B/C/S translation to be found on transcript pages 33364 through 33367. On 27 March, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that a new translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID M001-2055-BCST and requested its admission. If there are no objections by the Defence, and apparently there are not, and if it's a translation issue, then, of course, you always can revisit it, Mr. Lukic, on short-term. The Chamber therefore instructs the Registry to replace the existing B/C/S translation of P7227 with the new translation and admits P7227 into evidence. I move to P7242. On the 19th of March, P7242 was marked for identification, pending the provision of a complete copy of the original document and a revised B/C/S translation. Transcript pages 33425 through 33429. On the 15th of April, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence that document P7242, as currently uploaded into e-court, is the only version the Prosecution has in its possession and that the existing B/C/S version includes a translation of the legible portions of the document. Consequently, the Prosecution requests the admission of document P7242 as it currently exists. The Chamber has not heard yet from the Defence on this matter. If there's no objection, and I hear of none, the Chamber hereby admits P7242 into evidence. I move to P7250, P7251, and P7252. On the 23rd of March, P7250, 7251, and 7252 were marked for identification pending English translations, transcript pages 33512 through -513. On that same day, the Defence stated that once the translations were provided it would not object to their admission. On the 15th of April, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence that revised translations of documents P7250, P7251, and P7252 had been uploaded into e-court under documents ID 0429-2654-ET, ID 0436-6230-ET, and ID 0431-6085-ET respectively. The Chamber instructs the Registry to attach the new translations and hereby admits P7250, P7251, and P7252 into evidence. Videolink still not being properly restored, I continue with remaining issues from the testimony of Savo Sokanovic. I start with P7391. During the testimony of this witness on the 18th of May, the exhibit number P7391 was reserved for excerpts of the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 19225, a collection of five magazine articles. Only two of these articles were used during the testimony of Sokanovic. On the 18th of June, the Prosecution advised the Chamber that it has uploaded the two articles into e-court as documents bearing Rule 65 ter number 19225a and requested to replace P7391 with this document. I see that there are no objections from the Defence. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the current P7391 with document bearing Rule 65 ter number 19225a and admits P7391 into evidence. I move to D1059 which was marked for identification during the testimony of Savo Sokanovic on the 18th of May, pending English translation. On the 29th of June, the Defence e-mailed the Chamber and Prosecution and advised that the translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 1D19-2319. The Chamber instructs the Registry to attach this translation and admits D1059 into evidence. P7196. These transcript excerpts from the 22nd Session of Republika Srpska Assembly were admitted on the 9th of April, 2015, into evidence as Exhibit P7196. During the testimony of Savo Sokanovic on the 18th of May, additional excerpts of this transcript were used. On the 26th of May, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and Defence and advised that it had added these excerpts to the excerpts admitted as P7196 and uploaded the combined excerpts into e-court as document bearing Rule 65 ter number 02362b. The Prosecution requested in this e-mail this document to be admitted. I hear of no objections from the Defence. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the current P7196 with document Rule 65 ter number 02362b and admits it into evidence. Next item is the remaining issue from the testimony of Nedjo Vlaski. On 5th of November of last year during the testimony of Nedjo Vlaski, D745 was marked for identification. The Prosecution at that time objected to the admission on the grounds of lack of provenance and lack of foundation through the witness. The Defence then stated that it would seek admission when it was able to provide the Prosecution with information about the document's origin. As a result of the Defence remaining silent on two occasions when the Chamber asked it whether it still intended to seek admission of D745, the Chamber, on the 14th of May of this year, denied admission without prejudice and gave the Defence a week to revisit the matter. On the 20th of May, the Defence e-mailed the Chamber and the Prosecution and advised that Vlaski, and I quote, "confirmed that the document was provided to him by the Serbian security service." Is the Prosecution in a position to make a further submission with regard to the provenance and consequences for its position as far as admission of D745 is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll have to consult and we'll get back to you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from you. And after having heard, we'll consider whether the matter is ripe for being decided. Then the next item -- is there any way that the ... efforts to make a call should not reach our earphones? Not to say that one should stop trying, but if it can be down without hearing it, that would be appreciated. The next one is documents listed as associated exhibits to Rule 92 ter statement of Milenko Karisik. On the 26th of January of this year, the Defence filed a motion for the admission of the statement of Milenko Karisik. The motion also contained a request for the addition of a number of documents to the Defence's Rule 65 ter exhibit list as well as their admission into evidence. Among them were documents bearing Rule 65 ter numbers 1D5310, 1D5311, and 1D5312. Ultimately, the Defence did not request their addition to its Rule 65 ter list and admission into evidence during the witness's testimony on the 16th and the 17th of March. For the benefit of a clean trial record, the Chamber hereby notifies the Defence that it considers the Defence's requests in relation to these documents withdrawn if it does not hear from the Defence by the 30th of July of 2015.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the next item, we should briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Next item deals with translation of P7372. This exhibit was marked for identification on the 7th of May of this year, pending an English translation. On the 20th of May, the Prosecution advised that a translation was ready and indicated that it would request attachment and admission. On the 21st of May, the Defence objected to the translation by e-mail. The Chamber invites the parties to reach an agreement on the translation within two weeks from today and to inform the Chamber of this. If an agreement cannot be reached within this time, the parties are directed to make their submissions on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I move on to a few remaining issues from the testimony of Branko Basara. On the 24th of April of this year, the Prosecution notified the Chamber and the Defence that it intended to offer into evidence two documents through Witness Basara, document bearing 65 ter number 27968a for which exhibit number P7322 was reserved, and document bearing 65 ter number 31876a. On the 18th of May, the Prosecution requested admission of P7322 and document bearing 65 ter number 31876a for which P7389 was reserved on that same day. The Chamber granted the Defence until the end of May to raise objections, if any, and this can be found at transcript pages 35671 through -73. As of today's date, the Defence has not articulated any objections. The Chamber therefore admits P7322 and P7389 into evidence. Next item is the remaining issue from the testimony of Goran Dragojevic. During his testimony on the 14th of May of this year P7387 was marked for identification pending a translation into English. This can be found at transcript page 35639. On the 9th of June, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that a translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID number 0146-7733-1-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the translation and admits P7387 into evidence. As always, Mr. Lukic, if there's any problem with a translation, you can revisit the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I've still a few matters on my agenda, I think we should first take a break and we will resume. And Mr. Registrar at this side of the videolink is invited to communicate by whatever means with the persons at the far end of the videolink that we'll resume at 20 minutes past midday. We take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the videolink is functioning well now again. Let's just test it. Mr. Registrar at the far end of the videolink, can you hear me and can you see us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour, I can hear you and see the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we can see and hear you as well. However, before Mr. Lukic will continue the re-examination, I'd like to briefly deal with time estimates. Could you tell us approximately, where you said you need a lot of time, how much time you'd need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought that I would be able to see how it develops. I have a lot of questions, really. I will try to be as concise as possible, but at least five hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would mean that, Mr. Traldi, any --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to put on the record that there hasn't been a re-examination significantly longer than an hour and a half in this trial to this point, that adding up the Prosecution's re-directs, for instance, on Witnesses Butler, Brown, Higgs, Donja, and Theunens with a net cross of about 26 hour, four times the cross of this witness, we did about three, three to four hours total re-direct for those five witnesses, and I'd submit it's not an appropriate use of re-examination, to spend five hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before I make further observations, do you wish to respond to what Mr. Traldi said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, so many documents were opened and shown to this witness, and of course we are not going through every single one, but I have to challenge the presentation made by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, at the very beginning of the testimony of this witness I already have drawn your attention to the fact that you present this witness - and it's not for the first time - giving, well, rather general statements about a multitude of matters without giving proper sources. Those matters you've dealt with in the presentation of this witness. So therefore, they're not triggered by the cross-examination. The cross-examination took a long time, but I would say that one could understand that it took such a long time, because if you say in Kotor Varos there was never anything like a plan, you raised the issue about the plans of removal in Kotor Varos. You didn't give any sources, et cetera, so the Prosecution thought that they would have to respond to that in cross-examination. But it's not a matter raised in cross-examination, it's a matter raised in-chief by introducing evidence which is lacking any detail. But the subject matter was part of the examination-in-chief, and re-examination is to respond to matters triggered in cross-examination. Now I'm not saying that this Chamber finds that you should not have -- well, that you should not be given an opportunity to deal with some of those matters, but the way in which the whole examination of this witness is approached is asking for these kind of difficulties, and whether five hours will be granted, let's not at this moment finally decide on it. You're invited to focus on what you consider the most important matters. We'll then see what level of importance we will experience, rather than all kind of details which do not really affect what the witness said either in his statement or in cross-examination, and then at the end of this day we'll see where we stand, because this Chamber is intending to see whether we could finalise the hearing of the evidence of this witness and the next witness by Thursday, quarter past 2.00. If it would turn out that it's still of great relevance and despite the fact that most of the matters may not have been raised, at least the basic substance of it, by the cross-examination but rather by the way in which you presented your evidence in chief, if we would already give some additional time going over quarter past 2.00 tomorrow, we'll then consider whether there's any opportunity have an extended session on Thursday to see whether we can conclude hearing the evidence of this and the next witness by tomorrow, perhaps not at 2.15 sharp. Let that be of guidance to you and the credit you may expect also depends on how your re-examination develops. We'll now proceed, Mr. Lukic. I see the witness is putting up his earphones again. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General Kelecevic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You started explaining something but our communication was interrupted, and we did not hear it to the end. Please tell us when and why you left the command post at Vrelo between Prnjavor and Derventa.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command post at Vrelo was abandoned first and foremost because of shelling coming from the Croatian and Muslim forces in the general area of the command post. We moved the group some 5 or 6 kilometres away to the village of Strpci and I accompanied them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Strpci?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there until the beginning of June, I think. I don't know the date, but sometime in early June. The situation became more complex in the -- on the axis Brod-Derventa and on the axis Odzak-Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of communication means did you have at that command post and which ones were lacking?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part it was radio communication and shorter coded dispatches. We did not have those until mid-June when we went to Rudanka near Doboj. That was the third command post in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at Rudanka?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There we carried out a detailed assessment of the situation and proposals were made to -- for a decision by the commander, and many other things were prepared. We stayed there until the 20th of June, I think, when we went to the area of Trebava and Duge Njive. It is a village between Doboj and Duge Njive. The name of the village is Osecina. We were in the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there? What kind of equipment did you or did you not have?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Osecina there were already several commanders there who frequented the place, and all the necessary communication was there so as to be able to receive even longer dispatches. We were already preparing for the opening up of the corridor. At that time, enemy forces had already taken Derventa and continued towards Johovac and Foca. From the other side, from Odzak and Modrica, they had cut off the area around the 19th. They had cut off the corridor in the general area of Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until what time did you stay at Duge Njive?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there -- well, it was an observation post of sorts there which we reached from Osecina. Duge Njive is some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for the third time you ask about time he stayed there. The witness didn't answer [Realtime transcript read in error "witness answered"] that question. You should focus the witness and invite the witness to answer the question short and precisely. Otherwise, you will lose court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, if you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I said -- sorry, I have to correct my --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's wrongly entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I said the witness didn't answer that question. That was what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, until what time did you remain in Duge Njive? Perhaps you can tell us a date.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely. What I can tell you is that we stayed in Duge Njive until sometime in late November in Osecina. Then we moved to the town of Doboj and we stayed there until mid-December or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until what time did you stay in Doboj? And if you left, why?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing happened. Our command post was detected and targeted. Two of our soldiers were killed, and we were forced to move the command post to Prnjavor. In Prnjavor, the command post became operational sometime in mid-December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the command post in Prnjavor fully developed? Did you have the equipment you needed?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The command post in Prnjavor developed gradually to a full-fledged command post which remained there until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have P431, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have before us the minutes of an assembly session of the Serbian people in BH, the 16th session of the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 41 in English and 34 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Traldi quoted a portion of this, where it is stated that General Mladic said that "we're not starting from scratch," and then he quoted the text further. Let me ask you this: In your view, what sort of army was it supposed to be, the VRS? In your view, what was its goal?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the VRS had its basic task to preserve the Serb people and territory, as well as the citizens who wished to remain in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, and you spent the war there, was the plan to occupy territory or hold onto territory which was not considered Serbian?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No such plan existed. The plan was, as I said, to maintain the territory where the Serbs were in the majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Following the part that was read out to you, it is rather difficult to find it in this densely typed text in B/C/S.
