utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In the English, it's somewhere in the middle here, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "That is a very important. Our starting point are the armed Serbian people," and then goes up to "phantom Ustasha dragon."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the page the line begins with the words "wiped out," and then it continues by saying: "We are not going ..." That is what I intend to read. It is line 13 in the B/C/S. General, I will read it out for you.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's difficult for me to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is ascribed to General Mladic: "We are not going to create a conquering army. That is my proposal. We do not want a conquering army. We do not need what is not ours. We are creating an army which will defend successfully the traces our fathers have left behind and protect our children from the conquering ambitions of Nazi mercenaries which will bring freedom to its people and enable it to live in peace and serenity in its environment and its centuries'-old hearths." We have a problem it seems with the translation at the end of the sentence, because in English we have -- we think that instead of "hearths" the translation should read "hearthstone." The next question, General. You were asked about the strategic goals. You said that you don't remember how you learned about those precisely. We can find it at transcript page 37136, lines 1 through 8. In your view, what was the strategic goal of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The strategic goal of Republika Srpska was as I said, i.e., preserve the Serb territory, the Serb people, and make it possible for all those who wished to live and work there to do so while respecting the authorities of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At transcript page 37136, you were asked about the first and second strategic goals together. My learned friend Traldi asked you as follows, and I'll read it out, and you can you listen to the translation. [In English] I quote: "Q. And the objectives that you learned of, those included, most importantly, for the 1st Krajina Corps separation from Muslims and Croats and the establishment of a corridor connecting the Bosnian Krajina with the eastern part of Republika Srpska through the Posavina region; right? "A. That was the task, but I wouldn't say that we had to establish a corridor." [Interpretation] And then you continue about the corridor. However, for the time being, we're going to leave the corridor aside, and this is what I'm going to ask you. The first strategic objective that the Prosecutor asked you about, the separation of Muslims and Croats, was that discussed? What was your understanding of this, if you've heard of this strategic objective?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that unambiguously that is how I understood this objective, I mean, but I know the idea of my commander; namely, that the objective was that we are not separated in this harsh sense. I repeat that. But that those, I repeat, who wished to live in the area of Republika Srpska can live there, and that is my view to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one follow-up question. Are you telling us that the strategic goals, as you understood them, are different from the ones as formulated for the Republika Srpska, or did have the army its own version of the strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a big difference. The essence of that answer would be the essence. There doesn't have to be a strict separation of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, did you have a different one? Whether the distinction was big or small, we'll consider that. But does it mean that you were not fully in line with the strategic goals as formulated and published for the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was for these strategic goals, but I tried to explain it in a bit more detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not an answer to my question, but Mr. Lukic may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at how General Mladic saw this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it's page 9. In the B/C/S version, it is page 8. I cannot see it in the English version. In the B/C/S version, it is the very top of the page. [In English] Probably it's the previous page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm not sure what Mr. Lukic is pointing towards, but I'd just ask first if he clarify who he is representing the speaker is in this portion of the assembly session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My understanding is that General Mladic is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you have the right page, we'll be able to verify that on the basis of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually this is Karadzic, sorry. This is Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's Mr. Karadzic. Okay. Then, is it still relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the bottom of the page, please. Then go to the next one in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which strategic goal you're looking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English it's second paragraph, but it's a bit different from the B/C/S. The second -- before the second. [Interpretation] It is line 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just start reading slowly, Mr. Lukic, we may be able to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm. [Interpretation] "Separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with such practices if we were to stay together in the same state." Mr. Kelecevic, do you have any knowledge as to how your colleagues from the 1st Krajina Corps understood this strategic goal, if they knew about it at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That strategic goal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic first finishes his question, then you may object, Mr. Traldi. And the witness is invited not to answer until we have dealt with it. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I finished my question Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You finished your question. Then, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't object to Mr. Lukic drawing the witness's attention to any portion of the speech. But if he's going to be representing that this describes the strategic goal, then he should read the part beginning at the words: "The first such goal is..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least's that's what you invite him to do --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as least to avoid any confusion. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S, it -- it begins as I read, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S it's top of the page. It's easily to be checked. The first paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English -- that's why I said in English it's a bit different. The paragraph is a bit differently composed. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I can accept that it's the first strategic objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the first strategic objective?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Separation of our enemies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Put the question to the witness. You have put a text to him. And if there's any further need to deal with that, you have an opportunity to do so, Mr. Traldi. Please put the question to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Kelecevic, did you talk to your colleagues and what was their understanding, and did they know about this strategic goal before 1993 when it was published in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That strategic goal was understood by most officers of the corps as I said originally. Those who were ready to live together with the Serb people and to follow the same policy, of course, naturally they should stay in the same state. In my view, that is the essence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, perhaps we should ask the witness. What state would that be that you would then stay in together? Witness, could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That state would be, first of all, Republika Srpska and where most of the Serb people live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is how you understood, your colleagues understood the first strategic goal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is how we understood it, of course. We were not avoiding our mother state, the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before you proceed. When Mr. Traldi asked you to start somewhere, you said that where you started was the beginning of the first goal as you -- as it's written in the B/C/S. Now, there is a sentence in the English which I would like to check with you if it's not there the Serbian -- in the B/C/S, and if it is not there then it raises the question of a translation. Before that sentence that you started from, there is a sentence that says: "The first such goal is separation from the other two national communities. Separation of states." Do you have that sentence in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the previous page, Your Honour. On this page, I read what is in this paragraph on this page on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read that sentence now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay -- no, no, no. If it's there, that's fine. Because that was what Mr. Traldi was trying to draw your attention to. That's where the first goal starts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: See, now we went back one page and paragraphs are differently divided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S those were two paragraphs, in English only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there is no disagreement any further on what the text says on whatever page it may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read out what I did not read out a moment ago. So we went one page back in B/C/S, the last paragraph on this page in B/C/S, and it is the second page -- the second paragraph on this page in English. This is what is written there. I quote: "The Serb side in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Presidency, the government, the Council for National Security which we have set up, have formulated the strategic priorities of the Serb people. That is to say, the strategic goals for the Serb people. The first such strategic goal is separation from the other two national communities, separation of states." Today do you understand what is meant by this separation of states? I don't know if you've heard the question. Do you have a position on that? Was this discussed in the Army of Republika Srpska what this means, "separation of states"?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Separation of states, well, I assume that the officers I communicated with then believed that this is first of all separation in Bosnia-Herzegovina if there is no other way of reaching agreement and living together. Separation of states was not meant to be separation from the Republic of Serbia. If you are asking me for the broader concept, where Serbs lived - in Banija, Kordun, Lika, Northern Dalmatia, Slavonia east and west - then Serbs were also supposed to live in those areas safely, securely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know when Alija Izetbegovic declared mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember the exact date --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If not, then we're not going to guess.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also it was put to you that General Mladic held inflammatory speeches at this assembly, referring to Ustashas. At that time and before that time - that is to say, before the 12th of May, 1992 -- actually, let us start with the elections in 1990 when the HDZ came to power. What were the symbols that were adopted by the Republic of Croatia; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Symbols, first of all, well, first of all, they changed the flag and the five-pointed star. They took the chess-board as the symbol of the Independent State of Croatia, and that is the symbol --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. The relevance of all this is still arguable. But, Mr. Traldi, is it the position of the Prosecution that the Croats would not have used inflammatory language and if -- would not have taken a rather nationalistic cause by emblems. Is that your -- is that the position or is there agreement that all parties may have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may respond to that. I think it would be easier if we kept it as narrow and concrete as possible. So there is certainly, to begin with, no dispute about the adoption of the chequer-board symbol at the time. Now, and I suspect -- I mean, Mr. Lukic could go on to other concrete steps or policies implemented by Croatian authorities that may or may not be relevant, and we could address those at once, but to go on to the characterisation and the impact might be more difficult. But, yes, there were nationalistic symbols employed by other sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- keep this in mind when you move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only the witness said, and I would like the transcript to reflect it, that in line 11, page 60: "And that is the symbol of Ustashas."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, now I'm going to ask you who Rajko Kovacevic is.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Kovacevic is a colonel in the command of the brigade in Bjelovar, the garrison there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that all you know of him, from the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did Mr. Kovacevic fair? What was his destiny?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I admit I don't immediately see how Colonel Kovacevic or the garrison in Bjelovar is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's complete example, it's not just a story, of what happened in Croatia, and this gentleman has, I think, personal knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still linked to the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I didn't cross-examine about Croatia in 1991 at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had inflammatory speeches, and those were not only speeches in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would like to put to the witness so that we can first find out whether there's any dispute about the matter with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to ask him about concrete actions of Croatian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I maintain my objection. This is in no way arises from the cross-examination I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, before we decide on the objection, are you aware of specific examples of inflammatory speeches by members of the Croatian or the Muslim community specifically in 1991, and could you tell us what you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like to say that the Republic of Croatia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no. I'd like you to answer my question. Do you have specific examples on your mind of inflammatory speeches such as this person said this on that occasion? And I'm talking about Croatian or Muslim inflammatory speeches.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am familiar with the speeches made by my commander, Martin Spegelj, who was arming and establishing an army apart from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. He is a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he's a Croat, but he was a general of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Where did he make such an inflammatory speech, if it was inflammatory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it doesn't have to be inflammatory, but he did hold such speeches in the area of Virovitica, the garrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I asked you to give examples of inflammatory speeches by Croats or Muslims and -- well, specific ones; that is, where and when, by whom, and what they said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. Right now I cannot give you exact examples, but I know, for instance, this commander who -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no. You've answered my question. Mr. Lukic, there's no dispute about similar attitudes taken by the other parties. The witness can't give us any examples. You're invited to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned the corridor in your testimony. What kind of information did you have before the operation of the opening up of the corridor was initiated? What kind of forces were there in Derventa, Brod, Johovac, meaning 60 kilometres deep into the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina across the Sava?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday or the day before I said that the Croat Muslim forces came from the north, from the Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely what you said. Croat Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Would the speakers not overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Croat forces came from the area of Slavonski Brod in Croatia, and of course it also included the Croats from Slavonski Brod. They also came from the direction of Odzak and Modrica. Let's make one thing clear: Most of the Croatian forces came from Brod and Derventa; and the Muslim forces came from Odzak and Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. As far as I understand, because Slavonski Brod means something else to us. You said Croats came from Slavonski Brod. What country is that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it is Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everything across the Sava is the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we seem to skip some things over every and now and then, for the record we need to have it perfectly clear and that is why I apologise for this clarification. You were asked about Colonel Hasotic and about the fact that he was replaced by Colonel Vukelic. What do you know about Colonel Hasotic's departure, was he driven away, did he leave voluntarily, did he retire, did he stay, and, if, so until when?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in the corps in March 1992, Hasotic was at the position of assistant commander of the corps for morale and political and legal affairs. He remained at that position until a certain date which I cannot recall now. In any case, he was in that position for at least a month while I was there. Later on, sometime in May - again, I can't be precise - Vukelic came in his stead. There are orders in existence that can be verified with the personnel department. I think he left because most of the fighters in the corps and the officers simply did not trust an officer in charge of morale to be someone of a different ethnicity. They considered a Serb to be appropriate, reflecting the majority ethnic composition of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At transcript page 37146, lines 7 through 10, you were asked about whether you know that General Talic and General Jokic were members of the Crisis Staff, and you said that you knew about Talic being on the Crisis Staff list, whereas you were not certain about Jokic. Do you know anything about the participation in the Crisis Staff, how often he attended the meetings, did he have the right of vote, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was a member of the Crisis Staff. He would go there when his tasks and duties permitted him to do that. He wasn't always there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I seek one clarification from the witness. Witness, you said that Hasotic was not -- because being a Muslim, he should not be in that position, commander of the corps for morale and political and legal affairs. Now, in your statement in paragraph 8 -- Mr. Mladic should not speak aloud. In your statement in paragraph 8, you say that colleagues were not treated differently because of their ethnicity, and you give Hasotic as an example. Now, at the same time you tell us now that because he was a Muslim he could not be trusted in that position and that therefore he could not continue to do that work. There's at least some friction between using Hasotic as an example of how no difference was made in relation to people of other ethnic origin and now telling us that because he was a Muslim he could not hold that position in a plurality Serb army. Any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. I assert that Hasotic lacked the authority and the confidence of the rank-and-file members. In addition to Hasotic, there was a brigades commander by the name of Smail Omic. After a while, he too asked to be relieved of his duty because he did not enjoy the full trust of his officers who were predominantly Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Hasotic asked to be relieved of his office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, Hasotic did not ask for it, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there because I try to understand the comparison you made. Please, the next question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at document number P3032.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is dated the 11th of May, 1992, with Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic's typed signature. Let me ask you about the preamble of the order. We are still dealing here with the 2nd Military District Command, a day before the VRS was formally established. It states: "... where needed in order to protect Serbian people and honest members of other nationalities in the Serbian Republic of BH and consolidate the operational position of units of the 2nd Military District ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at P7460 next. Command of the 5th Corps dated the 12th of May, the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This order is issued referring to the previous document, basically consisting of the same preamble: "For the purposes of protecting the Serbian people and honourable member of other peoples in the SRBH and also for the purpose of us strengthening the operational and tactical position of units of the 5th Corps ..." Later on, on the 17th of May, another document was issued, we will not show it, but it is P7122, it is something we have already seen, by the command of the 343rd Brigade. They followed up on the -- on this command of the 5th Corps command. What is your understanding of the term "honourable members of other peoples"?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've explained it several times already. All those who implemented the tasks aimed at achieving this idea of the Serbian people about living together with others. So all those who were in favour of co-existence with the Serbs and who were of military age and could be assigned to war units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're still on this document, I will jump forward and ask you something else about it so as not to have to go back to it later on. Let me ask you this: After the outbreak of the conflict, did the VRS forcibly mobilise members of the non-Serb population in the territory it controlled; if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, in item 2 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could we please have the reference on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads: "Make sure that all able-bodied conscripts of Serb nationality are conscripted" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is the next page, I'm sorry. I'll start from the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, in item 2, we see as follows: "Ensure that without fail all conscription-eligible persons of Serbian ethnicity are mobilised as well as conscription-eligible persons of other ethnicities if they wish to fight for the just cause of the SRBH's struggle."

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I said, at least the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could this be applied to the entire war?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once the mobilisation is concluded, it is finished for the time being, but there were several waves of conscription. Now, there were cases in the 1st Corps, if I may say --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's the break time, Your Honours, and because I have to move to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break now and we'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber understands that there's still have been technical problems but let's just test to start with whether you can see us and hear me. I again now seeing that you've put on your headphones, could the registrar at the far end of the videolink confirm that he hears me and that he sees us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, we have lost the English channel again, so I cannot hear what's being said in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll continue with procedural matters while waiting for the connection to the restored. Once it is functioning again, we'd like to be informed about it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honours. We have just been reconnected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and now you can hear me and see us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's continue, Mr. Lukic, and I wish you the best as far as connections with concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have P7122 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, before us is a document of the 343rd Motorised Brigade command dated the 17th of May, 1992, Prijedor. In item 1, we see that the following is being ordered: "The commander of the staff of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, core members of the command and documentation shall be relocated to the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks ..." Do you know how many TOs they're existed in May, June, and July of 1992, in Prijedor, all the way to September?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know precisely. I know that there should be only one Territorial Defence when talking about the municipal TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One of organisations. Let me ask you specifically: Do you know anything about a logistics base in Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think my objection has been over taken by the witness's answer, but I'd object to further questions in that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think that logistics base is beyond the scope of cross-examination. It wasn't raised. Again, it's -- depending on a further question Mr. Lukic asks, if any, I'll articulate it more specifically. But just that I'd ask that if another one comes up, the witness be instructed to wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, scope of cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since witness knows nothing about this, I will just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would ask to have P7325 on our screens. 7325. And all the questions will be in relation to another document which we are not going to open. It's P2874.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, have you been shown this document which was signed by the late General Gvero. I will skip a number of questions so as to speed things up. I will go immediately to the part that was read out to you by the Prosecution, which is on page 2 in both versions. In the English, it is the second paragraph; in the B/C/S, the third on this page, where some percentages are mentioned. It reads: "The state-building Serbian people," I will skip the percentages, "... must fight for a total partition from the Muslim and Croatian people and must create their own state ..." However, you were not read out the following which comes immediately after this part. "It is only then that they will be able to decide for themselves who to join with, whom to link up, and in what way. They do not want what does not belong to them, what has not been theirs for centuries, but they are not cede an inch of their territory." We have already discussed delineation along border-lines and ethnic lines. I wanted to show you the last paragraph in the B/C/S next, and it is also the last in the English. In the B/C/S, we will have to move to the next page after a while. It reads: "The Army of the Serbian Republic of BH is the army of the Serbian people of all loyalists and patriots and of all the citizens who are prepared to fight in its ranks for the just goals of the Serbian people, the defence of the republic's territorial integrity and peace in these parts." Let me ask you this: Do you have any information about whether anyone, ever, being non-Serb and wanting to join the VRS was refused by the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such case, but I do know that, for example -- would you allow me to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, yes. Briefly.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I do know that an entire platoon of ethnic Muslims in Derventa in the 322nd Brigade under the command of Djuharic, Captain Djuharic, also a Muslim, they stayed on in that unit up until the end of the war, and their name was Mesa Selimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like that finish with this document and then we're going to move onto the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 02775, please. [In English] Maybe it does have a P number, but I don't have it registered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 2775 has already been admitted as Exhibit P7463. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were asked on transcript page 37170, I'm going to quote the question and the answer, line 5. It is related to the distribution of weapons referred to in this document: "Q. [In English] Now, this is an example of the 5th Corps arming those subordinated Territorial Defence units that we talked about earlier; right? "A. Yes." [Interpretation] So please do focus on the date, the 5th of May, 1992. On the 5th of May, 1992, were TO units subordinated to the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already then they were, and we have already seen an order that regulated that. But let me say this, too: Most probably this has to do with the return of weapons to these units in Gradiska and the other ones from the warehouses, depots. Until then, that equipment was kept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, for instance, in Kotor Varos, whether the composition of the Territorial Defence was mixed at that time, the 5th of May? Were all ethnicities in the Territorial Defence or not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of one particular case, an officer near Siprage, that's near Kotor Varos, that he stayed on until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 5th of May, 1992. Do you know that there was a mixed Territorial Defence in Kotor Varos or do you not know about that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us look at P7464. This is an interview given by the late General Talic to Glas. Portions of this document have already been read out to you where General Talic says that nothing will be taken from the Krajina. And now I'm going to ask you the following: Do you know about any attempts of having weapons taken out, transported from the area of the Krajina at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any such cases. All of this equipment and weaponry stayed in the territory of the 5th Corps. I'm talking about the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll move on. In the same text, on page 3, we looked at it yesterday, there was a reference to the school centre Petar Drapsin and the Kosmos company. Do you know whether military facilities, industrial facilities, whether they remained in territory held by the BH army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that, I mean, in general terms, but I cannot speak individually about particular municipalities and so on. I am more familiar with the situation in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It will seem that you're saying something that I didn't ask you about. My next question: Do you know whether there was any military equipment, weaponry, and military facilities left in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that because I served there. Until the end of 2001, I was in the territory of Croatia. Everything stayed there. The entire structure. Only 240 tanks to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now let us look at P7467. Yesterday we spoke about this, this document. In the last paragraph it says: There is no official information about the purpose of General Adzic's visit. However, it is believed that ... and so on and so forth. Were you personally informed about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't. I see it's the 30th of April, and on the 30th of April I was already at this new post for two days, and then I stayed on there. But later on, I did hear that that meeting had been held.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On transcript page 37188, lines 8 to 13, you were asked about the establishment of operative groups. Why were operation groups established?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operation groups were established only for more successful and better command and control over units. I already said that the corps had 127.000 soldiers, 48 units. The front line was 1.260 kilometres long. It was manned from 27 municipalities and that that was only possible through establishing larger groups. That is operations group, tactical groups, and those were units that could be independent, and that was the only way in which there could be successful command and control over units. I don't know which commander could command 48 communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I was not aware reading the transcript that it was any issue for the Prosecution on why and whether for good reasons or not operation groups were established. Now apparently you focus on this, and I thought that was a totally different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought it would be just short answer. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- I mean, short answers or long answers, if it's irrelevant or it doesn't in any way challenge the evidence presented in cross-examination, then even short answers should not be there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On transcript page 37189 from line 17 to line 23, there was a reference to the command post in Manjaca. You said that that post at that time was not fully activated. Command -- or, rather, was the command ever there in operative terms?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection, based on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, it's not responsive to cross. The command and a command post are different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is -- should we not invite the witness to take his earphones off if you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take your earphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I put to the witness was that a command post was there. Asking whether the command was there, as in the corps command, doesn't I think arise out of the question I asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. That's why I want to establish that command was never there. Just command post, technically. But we have to know whether 1 kilometre from Manjaca camp was command of this corps ever or at that time. I think it's crucial. Command post means nothing. If it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said: "... I have to stress that command post at that time was not fully activated. It had a communications system and it had a security detail ... but the main command post was in Stara Gradiska."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I want to ask him whether at a later point in time, ever, a command of his corps or part of command of his corps was ever there. That's my intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Understanding Mr. Lukic's better, I'll withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please could the witness put on his earphones again. And I think it's to some extent implicit on what there was and what there was not. Please proceed. Use your time as you wish, Mr. Lukic, but don't be surprised --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will use at least half a minute to conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, General, at that location that we discussed, at Manjaca, and you said it was not fully activated, this command post, and that it had a communications system. At that time or perhaps later, was the command or part of the command of the 1st Krajina Corps ever there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the final operations in 1995 when the area of Mrkonjic Grad, Sipovo, and so on - I don't want to waste time by enumerating all of that - that command post was activated. That's the command post at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, the command post --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, at Manjaca. Was the command ever at Manjaca of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command was not there at all. It was just communications equipment, security, and the operations duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. That will be all for the day, so we will be troubling you tomorrow as well. We'll have to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll conclude -- could the witness put on his earphones again. We'll conclude for the day. We would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30, Witness. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way, with whomever, about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. We can now disconnect the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am moving fast since I skipped some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. What is the expectation so that we can look at it for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think session and a half, if videolink is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, having heard the re-examination as it developed until now, what would be your expectation if the re-examination would not change its character.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's a little bit hard to gauge because the scope of it is unprecedented in this trial, but I wouldn't say I have terribly much thus far. Ten minutes or less for certain, but I could be more accurate in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's try to work out a plan for tomorrow. Mr. Lukic, we will reserve the first two sessions to conclude the evidence of this witness. That's two hours. If the videolink is functioning well, that should do. We would then finish at 11.50. We'd resume at 10 minutes past 12.00 with the next witness, and I think all together the evidence of that witness should not take more than two hours. Half an hour and one hour. That's one hour and a half. That leaves some time. That would bring us to, most likely, 2.30. The Chamber wants to deliver quite a number of decisions and needs approximately 30 to 40 minutes for the remainder. Perhaps a little bit less because we've done already quite a bit with it. We'll try to arrange for an extended session tomorrow and trying to finish not later than half past 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For evidentiary matters, probably we don't need Mr. Mladic for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. For the?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For evidentiary matters probably we do not need presence of Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean procedural matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Procedural, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mladic is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll consult with him soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if he waives his right to be present. If we get to the details of D so-and-so numbers, then I leave it entirely in the hands of the Defence whether such a waiver will come or not. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 16th of July, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of July, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
